+`Char`/range work unblocked the port.
+
+**Slices 2–4 widened the vocabulary, each fixpoint-locked with teeth:**
+
+- **Slice 2 — comparison + word operators.** `< > <= >= == !=` (two-char
+  longest-match via `[a, b | rest]` peeking) and the word-operators
+  `and or not in rem div` (which the reference lexes as `{:op, w}`, not keywords),
+  plus the full 16-keyword set.
+- **Slice 3 — string and char literals.** `"…"` and `'X'` scanned char-by-char
+  (`scan_str`/`scan_char`), the body rebuilt via `Prim.str_from_chars`, the char's
+  codepoint via `Prim.char_code`.
+- **Slice 4 — number lexemes.** A model change: `TNum` now carries the source
+  *lexeme* (a `String`), not a folded `Int64`, because the reference keeps the
+  text — `1_000` stays `1_000` — and applies `norm_num` (a bare exponent gains
+  `.0` and lowercases its marker: `1e9`/`1E9` → `1.0e9`; a decimal keeps its
+  marker, `1.0E9`). The scanner accumulates the lexeme char-by-char across
+  `lex_int`/`lex_frac`/`lex_exp`, mirroring `Rian.Lexer.@num_re`
+  (`\d[\d_]*(?:\.\d[\d_]*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?`). It agrees with the reference over
+  `_` separators, decimals, and signed/unsigned exponents (the slice-4 corpus +
+  a number-lexeme teeth test).
+
+**Next:** the jump from `expr_tokens/1` to the full **`tokenize/1`** stream that
+`Rian.Decl` actually consumes — **significant newlines (`{:nl}`), `;`, and the
+`@annot` lane** — plus escapes inside literals and brackets. That parity is the
+gateway to porting the *declaration* front-end, not just the expression lexer.
 
 ## The whole compiler as one Rian artifact

+  # NUMBERS (slice 4) — accumulate the *lexeme* (reversed) rather than fold a
+  # value, because the reference keeps the source text (underscores included).
+  # The grammar mirrors `Rian.Lexer.@num_re`:
+  #     \d[\d_]*  ( . \d[\d_]* )?  ( [eE][+-]? \d+ )?
+  # and bakes in the `norm_num` rule: a BARE exponent (no decimal) gets `.0`
+  # inserted and the marker lowercased (`1e9`/`1E9` -> `1.0e9`); a decimal keeps
+  # its marker as written (`1.0E9` stays `1.0E9`). `acc` is the reversed lexeme;
+  # `rev` + `Prim.str_from_chars` rebuild it in source order (portable, no FFI).
+
+  # integer part (no decimal point seen yet)
+  def lex_int(cs Vec(Char), acc Vec(Char)) Vec(Tok)
+  def lex_int([c | rest], acc) when (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '_' := lex_int(rest, [c | acc])
+  def lex_int(['.', d | rest], acc) when d >= '0' and d <= '9' := lex_frac(rest, [d, '.' | acc])
+  def lex_int(['e', s, d | rest], acc) when (s == '+' or s == '-') and (d >= '0' and d <= '9') := lex_exp(rest, [d, s, 'e', '0', '.' | acc])
+  def lex_int(['E', s, d | rest], acc) when (s == '+' or s == '-') and (d >= '0' and d <= '9') := lex_exp(rest, [d, s, 'e', '0', '.' | acc])
+  def lex_int(['e', d | rest], acc) when d >= '0' and d <= '9' := lex_exp(rest, [d, 'e', '0', '.' | acc])
+  def lex_int(['E', d | rest], acc) when d >= '0' and d <= '9' := lex_exp(rest, [d, 'e', '0', '.' | acc])
+  def lex_int(cs, acc) := [TNum(Prim.str_from_chars(rev(acc, []))) | lex(cs)]
+
+  # fractional part (decimal point already consumed) — exponent marker case kept
+  def lex_frac(cs Vec(Char), acc Vec(Char)) Vec(Tok)
+  def lex_frac([c | rest], acc) when (c >= '0' and c <= '9') or c == '_' := lex_frac(rest, [c | acc])
+  def lex_frac([e, s, d | rest], acc) when (e == 'e' or e == 'E') and (s == '+' or s == '-') and (d >= '0' and d <= '9') := lex_exp(rest, [d, s, e | acc])
+  def lex_frac([e, d | rest], acc) when (e == 'e' or e == 'E') and (d >= '0' and d <= '9') := lex_exp(rest, [d, e | acc])
+  def lex_frac(cs, acc) := [TNum(Prim.str_from_chars(rev(acc, []))) | lex(cs)]
+
+  # exponent digits (\d+ only — no underscores, no decimal point)
+  def lex_exp(cs Vec(Char), acc Vec(Char)) Vec(Tok)
+  def lex_exp([c | rest], acc) when c >= '0' and c <= '9' := lex_exp(rest, [c | acc])
+  def lex_exp(cs, acc) := [TNum(Prim.str_from_chars(rev(acc, []))) | lex(cs)]
 
   # a string literal: accumulate chars (reversed) until the closing `"`, then
   # rebuild in source order (portable, no host FFI). (Slice 3 — no escapes yet.)
